data.title: Ascendis Pharma Wins EMA Panel Backing for TransCon CNP in Pediatric Achondroplasia
data.description:
An update from Ascendis Pharma ( (ASND) ) is now available.

On October 16, 2026, Ascendis Pharma announced that the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use adopted a positive opinion recommending EU marketing authorization for once-weekly TransCon CNP in children with achondroplasia aged two and older with open epiphyses. The decision followed review of a marketing application supported by three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials and up to three years of open-label extension data, underscoring the depth of clinical evidence for the orphan-designated therapy.

A final ruling by the European Commission on TransCon CNP is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, which will determine whether the product can be marketed across the EU. If approved, Ascendis plans its first European launch of TransCon CNP under the brand name YUVIWEL in Germany in the first quarter of 2027, a milestone that would mark the company’s entry into the EU achondroplasia market and could broaden treatment options for pediatric patients with this rare growth disorder.

data.title: Cumulus Media Emerges from Chapter 11 with New Ownership
data.description:
Cumulus Media ( (CMLSQ) ) has shared an update.

On October 16, 2026, Cumulus Media emerged from a prepackaged Chapter 11 process as a privately owned company, having completed an accelerated court-approved restructuring that left day-to-day operations, audiences and advertisers largely unaffected. The plan canceled about $600 million of funded debt in exchange for all of the reorganized equity and $50 million of new senior secured convertible notes, materially deleveraging the balance sheet and providing a financial reset for the radio and audio group.

Concurrently, Cumulus put in place a new four-year, $100 million asset-based revolving credit facility to refinance its prior ABL, fund working capital and general corporate purposes, and imposed customary covenants and a monthly fixed charge coverage test that will shape its future financing flexibility. The company also adopted new organizational documents that create dual-class common stock, strengthen stockholder governance rights and designate Delaware courts as the exclusive forum for internal corporate claims, while moving to deregister its securities, suspend SEC reporting and keep its new equity and notes unlisted, effectively transitioning stakeholders from a public equity model to a tightly held capital structure.
